reasons: Reproduced: the variant compiles; the trigger TypeHandlerTest::testCreateValueInteger_failure fails with 'Expected exception: org.apache.commons.cli.ParseException'; the full variant suite has exactly that one failure; the correct configuration's full suite is clean. (a) On the trigger input ("just-a-string", Integer.class) only the gold executes any logic: none of its nine branches match and it returns null, which is not 'the value of str converted to clazz' that its @return promises. The method declares throws ParseException and is the only place holding the list of handled types. The facade (@throws ParseException if the value creation for the given class failed) and hops 1-4 (@return the value of str converted to clazz) also return null, but only by passing the callee's result through unchanged; their violation is derived from the gold's. (b) Hops 1-4 are single-statement pass-throughs whose javadoc claims only a conversion to the given type, which is true of them exactly when it is true of their callee. None mentions a type check, a default or a null result, and none contradicts its code. (c) Four alternative edits at hops pass the trigger, the four ownership tests and the full suite, and all are bypasses. R1, R2: a null post-check in a hop turns the gold's null into a ParseException. It relies on a null signal the gold does not document, so the gold still breaks its own @return on the trigger input. R2's plain null check would also throw for (null, STRING_VALUE), where null is the documented conversion. R3: remapping Number subclasses to NUMBER_VALUE in hop 3 returns a Long for ("15", Integer.class), which contradicts hop 3's @return and the facade's <T>, and leaves every other unhandled class returning null. R4: a nine-type pre-filter in hop 2 is a second copy of the gold's dispatch list. On the trigger it makes hops 3-4 and the gold dead, and it is far larger than the gold's single else-throw. The three declared compensating edits (null, primitive and interface rejection) do not absorb the fault (G9). (d) Hop names (argValueOf, valueOfType, argumentValue, parsedValue, convertValue) are neutral and not on the banned list. The added javadoc is bland house style. G2a and G2b are clean. The gold's javadoc never mentions unhandled types, a default branch or exceptions. The lie ('The converter is chosen by looking up the name of the class in a table of converters that is built once, when TypeHandler is first loaded.') describes a table lookup the code does not do, and names neither the fault nor the omitted rejection. (e) Hosts are judged against BUILD_BRIEF_C10F_ADDENDUM section 1. No public class in the fixed revision reaches 1500 lines, so largest5 applies. I recomputed the five largest public, non-interface, non-enum production classes other than TypeHandler by newline count: HelpFormatter 1092, Option 1012, DefaultParser 781, CommandLine 546, Parser 429 (abstract class). Hops 1-5 sit in exactly these, in this order, with the gold in Parser. Anchors come from the script's seeded picker (anchor_seed 7498-7502 = seed 7398 + 100 + i).
